content:
emily-support: FYI — FinNova reported a wave of 429s earlier this morning (05:12–05:18 UTC). They gave a short sample log with lots of x-request-id values. Can someone take point on evidence collection and repro? cc @kyle-eng @nat-ops

alice-finnova: saw repeated 429s calling POST /v1/embeddings at ~qps 18 for a ~2s payload. Example header they sent: `x-request-id: fn-req-0a7b` — attached a tiny log excerpt.

alice-finnova: sample lines:
```
2026-02-14T05:13:01Z POST /v1/embeddings 200 x-request-id=fn-req-0a7b
2026-02-14T05:13:02Z POST /v1/embeddings 429 x-request-id=fn-req-0a7c
2026-02-14T05:13:03Z POST /v1/embeddings 429 x-request-id=fn-req-0a7d
2026-02-14T05:13:04Z POST /v1/embeddings 200 x-request-id=fn-req-0a7e
```

kyle-eng: thanks — can you also paste the response headers for a 429? even one sample is enough. We want `x-request-id`, `x-rate-limit-limit`, `x-rate-limit-remaining`, and any `retry-after`/`x-rw-quota` headers.

alice-finnova: here's a raw 429 response they captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: fn-req-0a7d
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1676473980
retry-after: 12
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": {"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit"}
}
```

nat-ops: looks like a per-minute quota and they hit the window boundary; but the logs show a burst pattern — some 200s, then a short spike of 429s, then 200s again. Can you run a controlled repro for us and attach a HAR or a curl trace? Quick commands below.

alice-finnova: sure. we're not sure about the exact concurrency they used. We can reproduce approximate traffic. Sending HAR shortly.

kyle-eng: reproducibility steps to run from their environment (replace TOKEN):
```
# single-threaded quick repro (rate ~20 qps):
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s x-request-id:%{header_x-request-id}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "x-request-id: fn-repro-$i" \
    -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
  sleep 0.05
done

# parallel repro (bursty):
seq 1 40 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s x-request-id:fn-par-{}\n" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"t"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```

kyle-eng: also collect a HAR (Chrome devtools -> Network -> Save as HAR) or `curl --trace-ascii har-trace.txt ...` and upload along with the list of `x-request-id` values. We'll correlate with ingress and rate-limiter logs.

sara-oncall: adding a checklist —
- [ ] customer HAR / curl trace uploaded
- [ ] full request ID list (fn-req-... / fn-repro-...)
- [ ] client region + public IP (if allowed)
- [ ] time window in UTC
- [ ] config: endpoint, model, payload size

deploy-bot: autoscaler: detected spike in the embeddings pool at 05:12 UTC, scaled +2 nodes (policy: burst-backfill). :gear:

nat-ops: I'll grep ingress for `fn-req-0a7*` and post matching backend request IDs. If rate-limiter shows the client exceeded the sliding window we might see it, else we should inspect shard skew.

alice-finnova: uploaded HAR to the ticket and pasted a pastebin with 42 x-request-ids. link: https://paste.redwood.example/finova-har-42

kyle-eng: great. once you share the paste, we will fetch logs and produce a timeline (per-second counts + 429s). If we confirm the quota windows line up, we'll advise increasing burst allowance or smoothing client QPS. If not, we'll dig into token routing and shard allocation.

emily-support: thanks team — next actions: @kyle-eng to produce timeline, @nat-ops to map request IDs to ingress/backends, @alice-finnova to try parallel repro with `x-request-id` headers and attach curl trace. I'll follow up with the customer in ~1h.

alice-finnova: ack. sending the curl trace now. :thumbsup:

sara-oncall: noted and will document findings in the ticket.
